title: Picking a side or watching the keeper

items.stem: A kicker uses the 'pick a side in advance' strategy. What does the kicker do?

options.text: Waits for the keeper to move, then aims at the opposite side
Hits the ball as hard as possible and lets the shot do the work
Chooses a corner before the run-up and strikes it whatever the keeper does
Aims at the keeper's body to force a mistake on the shot

items.stem: Your coach tells you this keeper always dives to one side early, before the ball is struck. Which strategy fits best?

options.text: Watch the keeper during the run-up and place the ball opposite the dive
Pick the same corner you always use and strike it as hard as you can
Aim at the middle of the goal so the keeper cannot read your shot
Pick a side in advance and change it each time you take a penalty

items.stem: This keeper stays still on the line until the ball is struck, then dives. You try to watch the keeper and change your aim at the last moment. What is the likely result?

options.text: You see the dive early enough to place the ball away from it
The keeper reads your eyes, so the shot is saved however you aim
You gain accuracy because watching the keeper steadies your technique
You have no keeper movement to read, so you should have picked a corner

items.stem: In one sentence: what is the main cost of watching the keeper and changing your aim late in the run-up?
You have decided to pick a side in advance. Which plan best matches your goal of scoring consistently?

options.text: Plant well behind the ball and swing as hard as possible at the middle
Choose the corner first, then strike with a controlled swing toward it
Choose the corner, but look at the keeper just before contact
Decide nothing until the run-up, then aim wherever the keeper is not

items.stem: In one sentence: what is the main risk of picking a side in advance and ignoring the keeper?
